status.scope_reason: The company itself engineers and manufactures medical-grade thermoplastic polyurethane films (such as Faitgom) used for wound dressings, plaster backings, and incision drapes.
status.evidence: According to the Faitplast Innovative Brochure 2025, the company manufactures Faitgom polyurethane TPU films used for wound dressings, plasters, and incision drapes.

claims.claim: The company reports its healthcare portfolio in the Faitplast Innovative Brochure 2025, which showcases a specialized selection of thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) films under the Faitgom and Faitex brands—such as Faitgom G272, Faitgom G716, Faitgom G2161, Faitech 2128, and Faitex 05—specifically engineered for incision drapes, plasters, and wound dressing applications with variable moisture vapor transmission rates (MVTR).

The company reports that it holds foundational technological patents dating back to 1975 for the production of its first multi-layer coextruded films, which were subsequently advanced in 1980 to engineer complex multi-layer structures containing barriers to gas, humidity, and light for the food packaging and medical industries, as documented by Fait Plast S.p.A.
claims.corrected: The company reports that it holds foundational technological patents dating back to 1965 for the production of its first multi-layer coextruded films, which were subsequently advanced in the 1980s to engineer complex multi-layer structures containing barriers to gas, humidity, and light for the food packaging and medical industries, as documented by Fait Plast S.p.A.
claims.source: Faitplast Company Website (History/Chi Siamo) and Techtextil 2026 Exhibitor Profile

claims.claim: The company reports that its "Easy System" and "Faitgom" product families utilize custom thermoplastic extrusion and calendering technologies to engineer specialized multi-layer and skin-effect medical films, including aliphatic, polyester, and polyether-grade thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) films that can be processed through heat, calender, hot-melt, or solvent lamination, as detailed by Fait Plast S.p.A.
claims.source: Faitplast Official Website (Faitgom and Easy System Product Pages)

claims.claim: The company reports in its official 2025 innovative product brochure that its high-performance medical films and laminates, such as the Faitgom and Faitech families used for wound dressing and incision drapes, are compatible with standard medical sterilization methods.

A 50-µm-thick TPU foil manufactured by Fait Plast in Cellatica, Italy, was implemented as a sealing component for a laparoscopic SPOT manipulator system in an academic case study published in the journal International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery.
claims.source: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery (Springer)

claims.claim: The company reports in its Innovative Brochure 2025 that it provides a specific product matrix for wound dressing, plasters, and incision drapes including customized thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and hydrophilic membrane grades like Faitgom G272, Faitgom G716, Faitech 2128, and Faitex 01, which are customizable in thickness, shades, and moisture vapor transmission rates (MVTR).

The company reports that its Tech Center operates a dedicated research and development department to engineer new customized solutions and co-develop thermoplastic films tailored to specific client application parameters, including custom adjustments to the melting point difference between layers for specific double-layer films.
claims.note: custom adjustments to the melting point difference between layers for specific double-layer films

claims.claim: The company reports in its historical corporate summary that it completed an expansion in 1985 to increase coextrusion technology for producing multilayer films with barriers to gas, humidity, and light for advanced packaging, medical, and industrial fields.
claims.corrected: The company reports in its historical corporate summary that it completed an expansion in 1985 to increase polypropylene packaging technology for advanced packaging, medical, and industrial fields.

claims.claim: The development and manufacturing of specialized medical film product lines, including FAITGOM polyurethane films, FAITECH technical films, and FAITEX breathable membranes engineered for wound care dressings, plasters, and incision drapes, as documented in the Faitplast Innovative Brochure 2025.

The strategic acquisition of the company by Pennel & Flipo in August 2017 to expand technical thermoplastic film capabilities for the medical, paramedical, and orthopedic sectors, followed by its integration into the Michelin Group in 2024, as reported by Specialty Fabrics Review and Messe Frankfurt.
claims.corrected: The strategic acquisition of the company by Pennel & Flipo in June 2017 to expand technical thermoplastic film capabilities for the medical, paramedical, and orthopedic sectors, followed by its integration into the Michelin Group in 2023, as reported by Specialty Fabrics Review and Messe Frankfurt.
claims.source: Specialty Fabrics Review, Michelin Official Press Releases, IDI External Growth Reports
